newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heating oil ends lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heating oil ends lower on profit-taking.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil ended lower Friday in a late bout of profit-taking after bullish weather forecasts had propped up the oil complex for most of the session.
"Heating oil is where most of the longs bailed out," said Jim Ritterbusch, a trader with Sweeney Oil.

December heating oil ended 1.06 cents lower at 72.79 cents a gallon. Prompt heating oil had risen as high as 74.90 cents on forecasts by several weather services that there will be below normal temperatures next week for many regions in the United States.
December gasoline finished up 0.76 cent a gallon at 67.80 cents since dealers bought gasoline when heating oil weakened, traders said.
January crude ended nine cents lower at $23.75 a barrel.

Traders said that market participants began to be less worried about forecasts of colder weather over the next week to 10 days on reports that diplomats saw some momentum picking up toward implementing the Iraq-United Nations oil-for-food deal.
Under the deal, certain sanctions would be lifted by the United Nations against Iraq, allowing Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil in exchange for humanitarian aid.
With the Organization of Petroleum Producing Countries (OPEC) meeting in Geneva next week, traders said the market would continue volatile.
"The seesaw market is going to continue next week due to these political crosscurrents," said Ritterbusch.
Traders are expecting a rollover of OPEC's self-imposed 25.03 million barrel per day production ceiling.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
